newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP iron plant project hit by strike.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP iron plant project hit by strike.

text.p: A strike by up to 700 workers on Thursday has halted construction of a A$1.5 billion iron ore processing plant being built for The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd at Port Hedland, Western Australia, an official of the project's contractors group said.

Workers from three unions voted to walk off the job indefinitely on Thursday over wage and benefits disputes and are not planning to return until a workers meeting is held on January 15 at the earliest, Christoper Mitsopoulos, representative for the Chamber of Commerce and Industry contractors group told Reuters from Perth.

The workers, belonging to the metal workers, electrical workers and crane drivers' unions are claiming their pay is inadequate to meet cost-of-living expenses in the town, and they want up to 38 percent above the current award rate, Mitsopoulos said.
"There are also benefit issues they want addresed," he said.
A spokesman for BHP said the workers' complaints were not aimed at BHP and that the project remained about a year away from completion.
"It is between the workers and the independent contractors," he said.
The plant is being designed to produce hot briquetted iron pellets, which are used as high-grade substitutes for scrap metal in steelmaking.
